# Cyclorite
Cyclorites are a notably tall species of humanoid arthropods with a rocky shell and equally notable single large eye as their only noticable facial feature.
## Racial Features - They breathe nitrogen. - Their blood is [color=#ffa500]copper[/color] based, thus being metabolised from it. - They are significantly more sturdy, [color=#1e90ff]falling into crit at 1290 damage and dying at 240 damage[/color]. - additionally, they move [color=#ffa500]15% slower[/color]. - Due to their size, they stretch external clothing to such an extent that they can fit two items on their back. - They take [color=#1e90ff]15% less blunt damage[/color] and [color=#1e90ff]25% less slash damage[/color]. - Their punches deal [color=red]13[/color] blunt and [color=red]10[/color] structural, however [color=#ffa500]they swing 50% slower[/color]. - Their standard body heat is 37 degrees Celcius and they can withstand temperatures between -15 and 50 degrees Celcius.
## Nightvision Cyclorites have a innate nightvision thanks to their eyes. This allows them to see in pure darkness farther than any normal lightsource would allow. They will have normal vision when wearing any equipment that provides flash immunity. Using HUD variants allows you to keep your innate vision, at the cost of losing flash immunity. You can configure if you start with glasses or HUD in the loadouts for all relevant roles.
## Flash Duration Due to their eyes being more sensitive to light, Cyclorites will be stunned for a longer duration when flashed. Flashes will take [color=yellow]2[/color] times as long as normal for other species, lasting up to [color=#ffa500]10[/color] seconds in the case of a localized flash.
## Terrum The Cyclorite language, known as Terrum, is composed of a series of vibrations and scrapes. it is often described as hard to understand and learn, requiring mechanical help to be spoken.
## Age and Names Cyclorites reach adulthood at about age 20, though it's not entirely clear when, if ever, they die of old age. Similar to lobsters from Earth, they just keep growing. They usually get their name early in life, but they don't have last names. On top of this, their naming convention is usually more abstract, concepts rather than traditional names.
